name: sol_mccc_9
description: Missing whitelist validation of source/destination chain IDs in cross-chain messaging
question: The source file in `source` processes incoming cross-chain messages or dispatches outgoing cross-chain messages using a chain identifier without validating that identifier against a whitelist or allow-list of supported chains, so messages from or to unsupported/arbitrary chains can be accepted or sent, leading to unpredictable behavior or fund loss; this excludes code that checks the chain ID against a stored mapping, enum, or allowed-list before processing, and excludes purely local/single-chain logic with no cross-chain messaging.
criteria: receiveMessage(uint256 srcChainId, ...) processes the payload immediately without checking srcChainId against any allowed set of chains
sendMessage(uint256 dstChainId, ...) forwards funds or calls to dstChainId without verifying it is in a supported chains list
A cross-chain handler decodes and executes an incoming message keyed only by sender address, ignoring the origin chain ID entirely
The contract maintains no mapping/array of supported chain IDs, yet accepts a chainId parameter from the relayer and trusts it directly for routing logic
